title.narrative: Reducing Marine Debris Program, Subprogram 1

description.narrative: Indonesia is the world's largest archipelago and among the largest contributors of plastic marine debris globally, with 5,000 tonnes of plastic entering Indonesia's ecosystems every day. Plastic pollution damages marine ecosystems, undermines coastal tourism and fishing livelihoods, and introduces microplastics into the food system. More than 60% of plastic waste is either not collected or mishandled with the majority being burnt in the open, this loss of recyclable material to the circular economy, and resulting improper disposal, directly contributes to resulting increases in greenhouse gas emissions (GHGs), and air pollution, and hinders the adaption of ecosystems to climate change. To address this issue, the Government of Indonesia has committed to an ambitious target of handling 70% of plastic marine debris by 2025 in a National Action Plan (NAP) for Handling Marine Debris. The Reducing Marine Debris Program is aligned with this action plan. A programmatic approach that combines policy-based loans, technical assistance (TA), and knowledge support was selected to support the government as it allows complex and ambitious reforms to be addressed comprehensively and enables ADB to support acceleration of the implementation of the NAP.

title.narrative: Policy 1 Outcome 1 Implementation Period: Jun 01, 2021 - Dec 31, 2023

description.narrative:
Action 1: The government approved with immediate effect, a law and regulation defining the responsibility of local government for collection of retribution fees and stipulating that fees collected should be used for the related service, to increase revenues and budget allocation for improved waste collection services. Target date: 2023-12-31
Action 2: Local governments commenced implementation of regulation mandating the use of digital payment systems to improve the efficiency of collection of retribution fees,d and MOHA directed local governments on appropriate budget allocation in line with the targets set out in the National Policy and Strategy on Management of Household Waste and Household-like Waste. Target date: 2023-12-31
Action 3: The MOEF approved, with immediate effect, regulation incentivizing good performance of waste banks and improved cooperation between waste banks, recyclers, and producers in line with 3R (reduce, reuse, and recycle) principles, and at least one local government issued guidance on handling of residual waste including diapers and sanitary napkins to reduce the impact of harmful items of marine debris. Target date: 2023-12-31
Action 4: The government approved the 2022 eNDC with an increased role of the waste sector in achieving Indonesia's climate change mitigation targets by raising the GHG emission reduction targets for the waste sector. Target date: 2023-12-31
Action 5: The MMAF approved with immediate effect regulation on pollution prevention which, (i) obliges any actors whose activities might result in pollution or damage to fisheries and the marine environment to prepare and implement prevention and rehabilitation plans, (ii) prevents fishing vessels from disposing of fishing gear in the sea and mandating the provision of waste collection facilities on board, to increase protection of the marine environment. Target date: 2023-12-31
Action 6: The MMAF implemented its commitment under the NAP by certifying at least 18% of targeted fishing ports as meeting international standards on waste management including on solid waste management and wastewater management. Target date: 2023-12-31
Action 7: The MMAF established and operationalized an assistance scheme for improved waste facilities and waste infrastructure for effective waste handling for communities in small islands and coastal areas vulnerable to the impacts of climate change, by providing guidance for communities on accessing government funds and offering capacity building assistance. Target date: 2023-12-31
Action 1: All local governments will issue regulation to implement revised responsibilities and principles on the collection and use of retribution fees for improved plastic waste management and at least two local governments will operationalize digital payment systems for more efficient collection of retribution fees for waste services. Target date: 2025-12-31

title.narrative: Policy 1 Outcome 1 Implementation Period: Jan 01, 2024 - Dec 31, 2025

description.narrative:
Policy 1: Plastic Waste Management System Improved Outcome 1: Plastic waste leakage into the ocean reduced by 58% (Baseline 2021: 440,107 tonnes/year) (Source: TKN PSL)
Action 2: The government will initiate legislative change for categorization of waste service as a mandatory basic service by approving the regulation initiative permit to mandate sufficient spending on plastic waste services for improved service delivery. Target date: 2025-12-31
Action 3: Waste banks will implement improved cooperation with retailers for reuse and refill initiatives to accelerate implementation of circular economy initiatives and implement appropriate handling of residual waste including diapers and sanitary napkins. Target date: 2025-12-31
Action 4: The government will commence implementation of the national long-term development strategy to 2045 which accelerates the implementation of a circular economy and targets zero waste. Target date: 2025-12-31
Action 5: The government will implement increased commitments on waste sector in the ENDC by (i) MPWH implementing regulation for the development of local government solid waste management master plans with enhanced government targets on waste management, (ii) MOEF commencing implementation of a roadmap for implementing Zero Waste 2050. Target date: 2025-12-31
Action 6: The MMAF will scale-up supervision and law enforcement against activities while pollute or damage fisheries and marine environment and implement mechanisms to reduce the disposal of fishing gear at sea. Target date: 2025-12-31
Action 7: The MMAF will fully implement its commitment under the NAP by certifying all remaining targeted fishing ports as meeting international standards on waste management including on solid waste management and wastewater management. Target date: 2025-12-31
Action 8: The MMAF will roll-out the Clean Coastal Village program to increase community action on the collection and recycling of plastic waste and establish waste free fishing villages and implement the restriction of single-use plastic by all coastal and marine stakeholders. Target date: 2025-12-31
Action 1: The government approved with immediate effect, a law and regulation defining the responsibility of local government for collection of retribution fees and stipulating that fees collected should be used for the related service, to increase revenues and budget allocation for improved waste collection services. description.narrative:
Policy 2: Problematic Plastic Production and Consumption Reduced Outcome 4: At least 13% of waste recycled at a waste processing facility by 2026 (Baseline 2021: 10%) (Source: SIPSN)
Action 2: The government will establish a nationwide scheme with a concrete roll-out plan for the collection of fees on plastic from producers, which is earmarked to finance improved waste management services and climate change or environmental initiatives. Target date: 2025-12-31
Action 3: At least 45% of all cities and regencies will approve with immediate effect regulation to ban or restrict the use of SUPs at the local government level to help achieve the goal of a complete ban by 2030. Target date: 2025-12-31
Action 4: The government in order to expand the use of recycling, reuse, and refill schemes will implement through, (i) BPOM a regulation to permit the sale of reusable products, (ii) MOI, the Green Industry Standards requiring a mandatory minimum recycled content for all types of plastics, and (iii) MOI, the revised national quality standards on food grade recycled PET and the guidelines for good manufacturing process. Target date: 2025-12-31
Action 1: The MOEF established standards and procedures for local government entries on waste generation and handling to operationalize the National Waste Information System (SIPSN) to enhance access to timely, accurate data on waste management for improved evidence-based policymaking for the sector. Target date: 2023-12-31

title.narrative: Policy 3 Outcome 1 Implementation Period: Jan 01, 2024 - Dec 31, 2025

description.narrative:
Policy 3: Data and Monitoring tools for Policymaking Strengthened Outcome 1: The percentage of cities/regencies reporting data to official government waste data platform increased to 71% (2021 Baseline: 49% (252) cities/regencies) (Source: SIPSN, MOEF)
Action 2: At least 10 additional local governments will adopt and implement gender budget statements for waste services to boost the inclusion of women in effective waste sector management. Target date: 2025-12-31
Action 3: The government will approve the second phase of NAP, with defined targets and timebound implementation plan, integrating lessons from the first phase of implementation, for continued progress on achieving the goals enshrined in the national action plan for improved marine debris handling. Target date: 2025-12-31

title.narrative: Policy 3 Outcome 1 Implementation Period: Jun 01, 2021 - Dec 31, 2023

description.narrative:
Policy 3: Data and Monitoring tools for Policymaking Strengthened Outcome 1: The percentage of cities/regencies reporting data to official government waste data platform increased to 71% (2021 Baseline: 49% (252) cities/regencies) (Source: SIPSN, MOEF)
Action 2: At least two local governments issued comprehensive gender budget statements to identify gender gaps in capacity building and the inclusion of women in effective waste sector management. Target date: 2023-12-31
Action 1: The government will improve the evidence base for policymaking by, (i) MOEF upgrading the SIPSN to improve performance management by cities and regencies, harmonizing SIPSN data with tourism and maritime data, and improving the collection of sex disaggregated data, (ii) MMAF expanding data collection and monitoring of plastic waste in coastal and marine areas. Target date: 2025-12-31
